review.brief_reason: Let A=(0.0069925...-0.0799144...*x3)^2>=0, B=(76.999...-0.0010000...*x4)^2>=0, and E be the Abs argument. E is a sum of positive-coefficient squares plus the positive constant 0.062999991151895205, so E>=0.062999991151895205>0 for all reals; hence Abs(E)=E exactly. The original denominator equals -(0.0054255...*A*B+0.0046888...*E+0.489999...), i.e. exactly the negation of the proposed denominator, while the proposed also flips the outer division sign; the two sign changes cancel, giving identical values. Both denominators are bounded away from zero (same zero set, in fact never zero), so domains coincide on R^5. Variables x1..x5 are unchanged and the Abs removal is justified by strict positivity, not by refitting constants.
